name: Hazaiah
overview: Hazaiah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Adaiah. His mention in Scripture is concise, with no additional personal notes or narrative details provided beyond his lineage. This brief record situates him within the post-exilic community of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Hazaiah means 'y-h-v-h sees,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's watchful presence. This proper name, as recorded in Nehemiah 11:5, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful declaration of divine observation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Hazaiah was the son of Adaiah. Additionally, it is inferred that Col-hozeh was his father, placing Hazaiah within a familial line mentioned in Nehemiah 11:5. Beyond these connections, no further family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hazaiah's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Judah during the post-exilic period. His mention affirms the continuity of the Jewish community as it resettled Jerusalem, highlighting the preservation of family lines important for tribal and religious identity. While the biblical record does not elaborate on his personal deeds, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of God's people in maintaining their heritage.
